title: A Transport-Information Framework for Continuous-Fiber-Aligned Coarse-Graining Representation Sets
abstract: Consider representation sets of interest whose elements are associated with continuous realizations related to them through coarse-graining (CG). CG can be regarded as an operation that reduces a representation by discarding information that is not retained in its output. However, a systematic description of the information structure associated with CG in general remains to be established. Here, we propose a transport-information framework for continuous-fiber-aligned representation sets, in which each representation is associated with a continuous realization through a fiber structure, with CG defining the projection onto the representation. Within this framework, CG is described through a local-map operation that transports continuous probability mass onto representative points. The resulting transport cost is expressed as the contraction of the second-moment structure of the underlying continuous representation with the transport metric. Building on the previously proposed framework of unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), this construction provides a non-arbitrary information-theoretic interpretation of the CG-associated transport cost in terms of information indistinguishability, quantified by an expected Kullback-Leibler divergence associated with the CG geometry. The present framework provides a basis for describing information costs associated with individual CG operations and for comparing representation sets while accounting for their underlying continuous realizations.
summary: This work introduces a Transport-Information Framework to systematically quantify the information cost associated with Coarse-Graining (CG) operations in continuous physical systems. It achieves this by equating the geometric transport cost, derived from the second-moment structure, with the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence. This provides a robust, information-theoretic basis for comparing different coarse-grained representations.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a systematic information-theoretic description for the information structure inherent in Coarse-Graining (CG) operations when applied to continuous physical representations.
main_result: It proposes a Transport-Information Framework that quantifies the information cost of CG using a combination of transport metrics (second-moment structure) and information divergence (Kullback-Leibler divergence).
method: The framework models the system using a fiber structure, describing CG as a local-map operation whose cost is calculated via the contraction of the second-moment structure with a transport metric, linking this to expected KL divergence.
model_or_system: The model involves representation sets associated with continuous realizations, where the CG operation projects the full continuous space onto a lower-dimensional representation set.

important_parameters: Second-moment matrix ($M_k$), Transport metric ($G_k$), Fisher information matrix ($\Omega_k$), and the parameter $\xi$ defining the local geometry.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes a correspondence between the representation set elements and their underlying continuous realizations via a fiber structure, and it relies on local approximations of the KL divergence.
paper_structure: The paper develops the framework by first defining the continuous-fiber structure, then deriving the local transport cost, and finally extending this to various comparison metrics, including pushforward comparisons for geometric objects.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between geometric transport costs and information-theoretic measures like KL divergence provides a powerful, non-arbitrary tool for quantifying information loss during coarse-graining, which is fundamental in many-body physics and statistical mechanics.
